features.note: The captures show a red facade threshold, front public band, long center spine, eight labeled room envelopes in a 4+4 arrangement, and a distinct rear-service strip. Rear openings and a separate corridor band are visible, although their direction and clearance are not equally legible from every view.

The global views show the intended 2 large, 4 medium, 2 small labels and modest envelope differences, and the Sala 3 pair shows tier blocks, a center aisle, a wheelchair void, a screen wall and a door. The pixels do not yet prove the three families independently through structural differences such as distinct tier counts, cross/side aisles, integrated bays, projection niches and entry/emergency openings; the labels carry too much of the distinction.

Facade glazing, the wider center entrance and aligned yellow accessible approach read clearly. Lobby/tickets, concessions and checkpoint remain adjacent, while the kitchen close-up visibly seats the vertical extract in collars at the hood outlet.

The engineering set distinguishes green RS-485, cyan dashed wireless media and a blue IP chain; the UG67 close-up visibly seats two vertical antennas and a contained Ethernet route. At whole-building scale, several green branches and drops disappear into visual clutter or appear to end in open space, so four complete terminal-origin trunks and fourteen terminal-ending drops cannot be verified from the saved pixels.

Most paired views preserve the same building and become usefully transparent in engineering state. The architecture UG67 capture is almost entirely an opaque wall/column close-up with no readable gateway, sockets or circulation context, and the wide engineering views compress endpoint attachments enough that the pair is not consistently reviewable.

important_features.note: Human proxies read coherently beside the glazed doors and the device close-ups retain small real-world scale rather than visibly inflating the devices.

The structural captures remain legible and distinguish bright shell views from darker auditorium views; final cinema lighting and surface polish are correctly deferred, but some dark engineering compositions reduce structural readability.

Kitchen extraction and the UG67 antenna/Ethernet roots show contact, and yellow junctions appear along the green routes. The set does not clearly prove roof supply/return root contacts, all wall sleeves, or every RS-485 endpoint termination, and several route segments read as suspended in empty space.

defects: The UG67 architecture capture is blocked by an opaque wall/column and contains no readable gateway or attachment context.

Large, medium and small auditorium families are identified mainly by labels and subtle envelope changes; the saved views do not visually prove distinct tier counts, aisle systems, wheelchair-bay integration, projection niches and paired entry/emergency openings across all three families.

The complete-network and neutral-engineering views are too distant and cluttered to verify four continuous UC-origin RS-485 trunks and all fourteen TC-ending drops; several green branches visually terminate in open space.
No saved close-up clearly proves roof supply/return plenum-to-main contacts, and wall-sleeve containment is not consistently readable.

Rear technical doors and the service strip are present, but the evidence does not unambiguously show each door opening into the non-overlapping 1.5 m corridor rather than merely existing on the rear wall.
corrections: Move the architecture UG67 camera in front of the interior wall plane and frame the gateway body, both socket collars, antenna roots, Ethernet port and adjacent circulation context without changing device scale.

Expose all three auditorium family masters in one comparable structural evidence view and make their geometry—not labels—prove large/medium/small differences: distinct tier counts, cross/side aisles, integrated wheelchair bays, screen walls, projection niches and entry/emergency openings.

Route each of the four green RS-485 trunks visibly from its UC terminal along a wall or tray, keep every junction in contact with containment, and frame all fourteen drops terminating at their assigned TC endpoints with no free-floating ends.
Add an evidence close-up that shows supply and return plenum-to-main root overlap plus the wall sleeves used by the routed services.

Reframe the rear technical band from above and inside the service corridor so the separating wall, continuous 1.5 m floor strip, thresholds, jamb depth and each door's corridor-facing opening are simultaneously visible.

mechanical.note: All 15 supplied console sidecars are clean. Probe medians are 106 draws and 12700 triangles against budgets of 550 and 750000; fps is informational only.
